## What it is

web<span class="webgeods-wordmark-geo">Geo</span>Ds brings spatial data analysis, interactive examples, and
free tools together in one place — Python and R side by side, running
entirely in your browser. Nothing to install, nothing uploaded
anywhere.

## Who it's for

For anyone whose work touches spatial data: checking whether a
dataset is actually correct, not just correctly shaped. Comparing how
Python and R handle the same problem, instead of trusting one
implementation blindly. Understanding a method well enough to know
when it applies, not just how to call it.

You don't need to be an expert programmer — the emphasis is on
spatial reasoning you can actually verify, not just read about.

## Why it's different

Most spatial data resources pick a side: Python or R. web<span class="webgeods-wordmark-geo">Geo</span>Ds treats
them as complementary — the same problem, shown in both, using the
tools each ecosystem actually uses (GeoPandas, Shapely, sf). Seeing
where they agree, and where they don't, teaches more than either one
alone.

**Your data stays yours.** Where a tool runs in the browser, your file
is processed locally — never uploaded, not even to us. That's not a
setting to enable; it's how the tools are built.

## What you can do here

Three things, connected:

**Read** — articles that explain a spatial problem properly, with
interactive examples built in, not just diagrams.

**Use** — free standalone tools for the same checks, when you just
need an answer, not the full explanation.

**Learn more** — the articles and tools are pieces of a larger,
ongoing effort to teach spatial data science end to end. Where that
leads next depends partly on what turns out to be useful — the
newsletter below is the way to follow it.
